data.title: Adapt a parametric chair to a size brief
data.summary: An existing chair generator, 0.45 m seat height and 0.48 m seat width. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: Geometry Nodes provides procedural geometry, instances and field-based controls.

prerequisites: An authorized Blender / COLMAP / Nerfstudio environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: An existing chair generator, 0.45 m seat height and 0.48 m seat width.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent parametric chair workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: An existing chair generator, 0.45 m seat height and 0.48 m seat width. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Inspect exposed generator parameters and reuse the nearest chair definition
Change seat height and width while keeping leg attachment points parameter-linked
Export one candidate and compare dimensions and floor contact to the brief

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned adapt a parametric chair to a size brief candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: All four feet touch the same floor plane
Measured seat height and width match the two inputs
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: A dimensionally correct chair is not certified ergonomic or structurally safe.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: Check the existing registry before adding a new chair ID.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me adapt a parametric chair to a size brief in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: An existing chair generator, 0.45 m seat height and 0.48 m seat width. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: All four feet touch the same floor plane; Measured seat height and width match the two inputs. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
